lede: Actor, producer and director across Tamil, Telugu, Hindi, Malayalam and Kannada cinema, with a career that spans three decades.

chapters.title: Mumbai
paragraphs: Simran was born Rishibala Naval on 4 April 1976 to Punjabi parents in Mumbai. She went to St. Anthony’s High School, Versova, and finished her twelfth year at Children Welfare Centre, Yari Road. Dance and drama ran through her school and college years.
She married Deepak Bagga, a childhood friend, on 2 December 2003. They have two children.

chapters.title: Debut and breakthrough
paragraphs: Simran made her screen debut in the 1995 Hindi film Sanam Harjai, directed by Saawan Kumar. She presented Superhit Muqabla on Doordarshan’s Metro channel, and was then offered a leading role in ABCL’s romantic drama Tere Mere Sapne (1996), remembered for the song Aankh Marey.
Her first break in South Indian cinema was the Malayalam film Indraprastham, opposite Mammootty. Her Kannada debut was Simhada Mari, opposite Shivarajkumar, and her Telugu debut was Abbai Gari Pelli.

Her Tamil debut came in 1997 with Once More and V.I.P. In Once More she played the lead opposite Vijay, alongside Sivaji Ganesan and Saroja Devi. In V.I.P. she was paired with Prabhu Deva, and their song Minnal Oru Kodi became a chartbuster. The two films won her the Filmfare Award for Best Female Debut – South. In Nerrukku Ner, produced by Mani Ratnam, she starred opposite Suriya in his debut.

In 1999 she played a blind woman in Thulladha Manamum Thullum, opposite Vijay, and received the Tamil Nadu State Film Award for Best Actress. Vaali, opposite Ajith Kumar, followed, and won her the Cinema Express Award for Best Actress – Tamil.

chapters.title: At the height
paragraphs: In 2000 came the Tamil films Parthen Rasithen and Priyamaanavale, and the Telugu films Yuvaraju with Mahesh Babu, Goppinti Alludu with Balakrishna and Kalisundam Raa with Venkatesh. In 2001 she concentrated on Telugu cinema: Mrugaraju and Daddy with Chiranjeevi, Bava Nachadu with Nagarjuna, and Narasimha Naidu with Balakrishna, an industry hit that earned her a Filmfare nomination for Best Actress – Telugu.

In Tamil that year she appeared in Jeeva’s 12B and in K. Balachander’s hundredth production, Paarthale Paravasam, with Madhavan. Of 12B, The Hindu wrote that “Simran does a commendable job in the climax”.

2002 brought Ramanaa with Vijayakanth, Pammal K. Sambandam and Panchathantiram with Kamal Haasan, Thamizh with Prashanth, and Mani Ratnam’s Kannathil Muthamittal with Madhavan, for which she won the Filmfare Award for Best Actress – Tamil.
At the height of her career, Simran took a break from film after her marriage.

chapters.title: The return
paragraphs: She returned in 2008 with Okka Magadu, John Appa Rao 40 Plus and Seval. Her role as wife and mother to Suriya’s characters in Gautham Vasudev Menon’s Vaaranam Aayiram won her the Filmfare Award for Best Supporting Actress – Tamil and the Vijay Award for Best Supporting Actress.

On television she starred in Jaya TV’s Simran Thirai, hosted the game show Jackpot in 2012, and in 2013 produced the reality show Dance Tamizha Dance with Deepak Bagga. In 2015 the two set up their production studio, Simran & Sons.

Guest and special appearances followed in Aaha Kalyanam, Trisha Illana Nayanthara, Koditta Idangalai Nirappuga, Thupparivaalan and Odu Raja Odu. In 2018 she played the antagonist opposite Sivakarthikeyan in Seemaraja, and in 2019 she starred opposite Rajinikanth in Petta.

chapters.title: Now
paragraphs: The Netflix anthology Paava Kadhaigal (2020) was followed by Mahaan, Rocketry: The Nambi Effect, Captain, Gulmohar and Tiger 3. Her negative role in Andhagan was critically acclaimed and brought further awards.
A special cameo in Good Bad Ugly introduced her to a new generation, and Tourist Family became a major box-office success, with wide acclaim for her performance. Dharman is now shooting.
